sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in New Braunfels, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. A direct cash sale in New Braunfels can close on your schedule, often within a few weeks, because no lender needs to approve the buyer. You give up some price in exchange for speed and certainty, so measure the offer against a listing estimate before you decide.

The city has been one of the fastest growing places in Texas. Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 122,492, a 35.5 percent rise from the April 2020 base. Rapid growth brings many new neighbors and many new listings, so a house that needs work competes with newer builds.

Typical reasons owners choose a quick sale:

  • Relocation along the I-35 corridor toward Austin or San Antonio.
  • An older home with repairs that financed buyers will not accept.
  • A short-term or vacation rental that no longer pays off.
  • An inherited house shared among several heirs.
  • A property with a code, title or tax problem.

sections.h2: How does New Braunfels work as a place to sell?
sections.html:
New Braunfels is the seat of Comal County, at the meeting of the Guadalupe and Comal rivers and Interstate 35 and Farm Road 725, thirty miles northeast of San Antonio and forty-five miles southwest of Austin, per the Handbook of Texas. The same entry says the city extends into Guadalupe County, so some parcels belong to a different county than the one the name suggests.

German immigrants founded the town on March 21, 1845. Its economy grew from mills, manufacturing and a commercial center, and later tourism: Landa Park, the rivers, Canyon Lake after 1964, Natural Bridge Caverns and Wurstfest. Those draws keep short stays and second homes in the market.

The Handbook also notes that the city is in the San Antonio metropolitan area, which is why many owners commute or sell to buyers moving from there.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about New Braunfels homes?
sections.html:
Values here run well above the state's small-city markets. The table below shows what Census QuickFacts reports for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $2,088, and 83.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. A stable, owner-heavy base like this means buyers have choices, and a visibly worn house is easy to skip.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and tax rules apply?
sections.html:
For Comal County parcels, the Comal Appraisal District values the property and handles exemptions. Its office is at 900 S. Seguin Ave., New Braunfels, with hours Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and its site highlights April 15 and May 15 as key dates. If your parcel lies in Guadalupe County, ask the tax office there who appraises it.

The state rules are on the Comptroller's site. Homeowners get a school district exemption of $140,000, and a homestead's appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year once the exemption has been in place, effective from the January 1 after it first applies. Owners 65 or older or disabled can have school taxes frozen.

  • Value date: January 1.
  • Protest deadline: generally May 15 or 30 days after notice.
  • Delinquency: February 1 after a January 31 deadline.

The cap helps long-term owners but resets for a buyer, so a recent sale can raise the bill for the next owner. That is useful to mention when you talk price.

sections.h2: Can I use a short-term rental or a rented house as a seller?
sections.html:
New Braunfels is known for river and lake visitors, so many houses have served as short stays. If yours is rented, the tenant's rights come first in the timeline. In Texas, a landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, then files in justice court if the tenant stays, per the State Law Library.

Ask the City of New Braunfels about any permit or registration tied to a short-term rental before you transfer the property, since requirements can differ from one address to another. A buyer who takes the house as is will want to know the rental history and any open compliance issue.

sections.h2: What if the house has a mortgage default or tax lien?
sections.html:
Act early. The State Law Library says a borrower has 20 days after the notice of default to cure it, and the notice of sale must arrive at least 21 days before the auction. Auctions are held on the first Tuesday of the month at the courthouse area set by the commissioners court.

Property tax liens are separate. A lien attaches on January 1, and after February 1 penalties and interest build up, with an added collection penalty of up to 20 percent if the unit hires a private attorney. Payoffs for both come out of the sale proceeds, so get the exact numbers from the title company.

sections.h2: How have growth and commuting shaped New Braunfels neighborhoods?
sections.html:
The city has repeatedly absorbed new land. The Handbook records that New Braunfels incorporated eight suburbs in 1947 and by 1990 reached into Guadalupe County, and its population went from 36,494 in 2000 to 90,403 in the 2020 Census. Land area was 45.18 square miles in 2020, up from 43.87 in 2010, and density rose from 1,316 to 2,001 people per square mile.

Residents spend 27.1 minutes on average getting to work, which is longer than in smaller Texas towns, and 98.0 percent of households have a computer. Those commuters often want a move-in-ready house near I-35 or Farm Road 725, so a home that needs updates may do better with an investor than with a typical family buyer.

Older neighborhoods near Landa Park and the river carry the city's German-era history, while newer subdivisions on the edge follow the growth. Tell any buyer which category your street falls in and whether your lot has flood or drainage history, since the rivers shape much of the town.

sections.h2: Which fast-sale option fits a New Braunfels owner?
sections.html:
The right path depends on condition and timing. A cash offer fits a house that needs repairs or an owner with a firm deadline, while a listing may net more for a polished house in a strong subdivision.

  • Cash offer: as is, owner picks the date, no financing contingency.
  • Traditional listing: higher potential price, plus commissions, repairs and showings.
  • Sale to an heir or relative: may need a deed and clear title paperwork.

Ask each buyer for a written offer and compare the net you would keep after payoffs and fees.

sections.h2: How does closing and recording work?
sections.html:
The title company prepares the deed and settlement statement, and the deed is recorded with the county clerk where the property sits. A deed must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer such as a notary to be recorded.

The County Clerk Manual lists the base recording fee at $5 for page one and $4 for each added page. Ask the Comal County Clerk, or the Guadalupe County Clerk if your parcel is there, for the current schedule.

faqs.q: How fast can a New Braunfels sale close?
faqs.a: Often in a few weeks if the title is clear. A shared inheritance, a lien or a tenant adds time. Request the closing date in writing with the offer.

faqs.q: Is New Braunfels in Comal or Guadalupe County?
faqs.a: Both. The city is the Comal County seat and extends into Guadalupe County, per the Handbook of Texas. Your tax bill shows which county's appraisal district applies.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in New Braunfels?
faqs.a: Census QuickFacts lists $339,400 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. Your own house's price depends on condition, location and size, so treat the figure as context only.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Braunfels house with foundation or roof problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase as is, and the offer accounts for repair costs. Compare it with a repaired listing estimate to see which nets more.

faqs.q: When are New Braunfels property tax protests due?
faqs.a: Generally May 15 or 30 days after the value notice, whichever is later, under the state calendar. The Comal Appraisal District site highlights April 15 and May 15 as key dates.
